content:
Let \(c\) be the number of chess players, so there are \(t=55-c\) tennis players.

Each chess player can have between \(0\) and \(t\) friends among the tennis players, so there are \(t+1\) possible friend-counts. Since no four chess players can share the same friend-count, each count can occur at most 3 times. Thus

\[
c \le 3(t+1)=3(56-c).
\]

So

\[
c \le 168-3c \implies 4c \le 168 \implies c \le 42.
\]

This is achievable: with \(c=42\) and \(t=13\), assign exactly 3 chess players to each possible friend-count \(0,1,\dots,13\).

\[
\boxed{42}
\]
